questions.question_text: A vacuum cleaner is rated at $1750$ W. What is this power in kilowatts?

options.why: Divided by $100$ instead of $1000$.
Divided by $10$ instead of $1000$.
Multiplied by $1000$ instead of dividing, so the answer is larger than the power in watts.

questions.question_text:
A $2.5$ kW water pump runs for $45$ minutes.
How much energy does it use, in kilowatt hours?

options.why: Used $45$ as a number of hours instead of converting $45$ minutes to $0.75$ hours.
Left the power in watts, multiplying $2500$ by $0.75$ instead of using kilowatts.
Divided the time by the power instead of multiplying them.

questions.question_text:
A $1.4$ kW appliance runs for $5$ hours.
Electricity is charged at $\$0.26$ per kWh.
What does it cost to run?

options.why: Multiplied the power by the price but never multiplied by the $5$ hours.
Multiplied the hours by the price and ignored the power rating of the appliance.
Divided the energy by the price per kWh instead of multiplying.

questions.question_text:
A $1800$ W kettle is used for $8$ minutes every day.
Electricity is charged at $\$0.30$ per kWh.
What is the cost of running the kettle for $365$ days?

options.why: Used $8$ as a number of hours instead of converting $8$ minutes to hours.
Converted minutes to hours by dividing by $100$ instead of by $60$.
Found the cost for a single day and never multiplied by the $365$ days.

questions.solution_text:
$1800\text{ W} = 1.8\text{ kW}$
$8\text{ min} = \dfrac{8}{60}\text{ h}$
$\text{energy per day} = 1.8 \times \dfrac{8}{60}$
$= 0.24\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy for }365\text{ days} = 0.24 \times 365$
$= 87.6\text{ kWh}$
$\text{cost} = 87.6 \times \$0.30$
$= \$26.28$

questions.question_text:
A classroom has $6$ heaters, each rated at $2400$ W, running for $5$ hours a day.
How much energy do they use in one day, in kilowatt hours?

options.why: Found the energy used by one heater and never multiplied by the $6$ heaters.
Multiplied the six heaters together but never multiplied by the $5$ hours.
Multiplied by the $6$ heaters a second time after the total power had already been found.

questions.question_text:
Running a $750$ W fan heater cost $\$9.45$ when electricity was charged at $35$ cents per kWh.
For how many hours was the heater running?

options.why: Multiplied the energy by the power in kW instead of dividing by it.
Left the power in watts, dividing the energy by $750$ instead of by $0.75$.
Multiplied the cost by the price per kWh instead of dividing to find the energy.

questions.question_text:
Dryer P is rated at $3200$ W and Dryer Q at $2600$ W. Each is run for $45$ minutes, $4$ times a week, for $52$ weeks.
Electricity costs $\$0.33$ per kWh.
How much more does Dryer P cost to run over the year?

options.why: Used $45$ as a number of hours instead of converting $45$ minutes to $0.75$ hours.
Left out the $4$ runs a week, costing only one run in each of the $52$ weeks.
Found the extra cost for a single week and never multiplied by the $52$ weeks.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{difference in power} = 3200 - 2600$
$= 600\text{ W}$
$= 0.6\text{ kW}$
$45\text{ min} = 0.75\text{ h}$
$\text{hours per year} = 0.75 \times 4 \times 52$
$= 156\text{ h}$
$\text{extra energy} = 0.6 \times 156$
$= 93.6\text{ kWh}$
$\text{extra cost} = 93.6 \times \$0.33$
$= \$30.888$
$\approx \$30.89$

questions.question_text:
A circulating pump is rated at $0.45$ kW.
What is this power in watts?

options.why: Multiplied by $10\,000$ instead of by $1000$.
Multiplied by $100$ instead of by $1000$.
Divided by $1000$ instead of multiplying, so the answer is smaller than the power in kilowatts.
